decisions.statement: Taking the hold is one create that fails if the hold is there.
The hold names the process that took the hold and the moment that process started.
A hold left by a process that is gone is taken rather than waited on.
A hold naming no holder that can be read is taken once the hold has been there too long.
A hold is released however the act inside the hold ends.
A hold is released only by the process whose mark is in the have.
A caller that never took the hold is refused.
A caller that never took the hold never has its act run.
The longest a caller waits for the hold is named for another caller to read.
The words a wait that ran out is known by are worded here rather than by a caller.
A wait that ran out is thrown as a kind of its own rather than as a plain error.
A caller asking for a refusal is answered a wait that ran out as a refusal.
That refusal states the code an operational fault exits with.
An act that failed inside the hold is thrown on rather than answered as a refusal.
Two landings over one worktree never overlap.

definition: the hold one landing takes over a worktree while it judges, writes and commits
